PLUMED is an open-source library for enhanced sampling, free-energy calculations, and analysis of collective variables in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. This page introduces the PLUMED repository, summarizes its high-level purpose, and provides a technical overview of its main architectural components and their relationships.

## Purpose

PLUMED is designed to be linked or interfaced with a wide range of MD engines (e.g., GROMACS, NAMD, LAMMPS, Quantum ESPRESSO). Its main roles are:

- Calculating complex collective variables (CVs) during MD simulations
- Applying biasing methods to enhance sampling of rare events
- Analyzing simulation trajectories and computing free-energy surfaces
- Integrating experimental data with simulations

PLUMED is modular, extensible, and supports both in-simulation and post-processing workflows.

Sources: [README.md:14-43](), [CHANGES/v2.8.md:1-30](), [CHANGES/v2.9.md:1-20]()

## High-Level System Architecture

**Diagram: PLUMED Core System Overview**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Build&QualitySystem"
        BuildSys["Build System (configure, Makefile, codecheck)"]
    end
    subgraph "CoreLibrary"
        CoreLib["libplumedKernel (src/lib/), Actions, CVs"]
        Wrapper["External Interface (src/wrapper/Plumed.h)"]
    end
    subgraph "Modules"
        Modules["Modules (Bias, Colvar, Function, Tools, etc.)"]
    end
    subgraph "CommandLineTools"
        CLTools["CLTools (driver, sum_hills, pesmd, etc.)"]
    end
    subgraph "Documentation"
        Docs["Documentation System (user-doc/, Doxygen)"]
    end
    subgraph "CI&Packaging"
        CI["CI & Packaging (GitHub Actions, Conda, Docker, MacPorts)"]
    end
    subgraph "PythonInterface"
        PyAPI["Python Interface (python/plumed.pyx)"]
    end

    BuildSys --> CoreLib
    CoreLib --> Wrapper
    CoreLib --> Modules
    Modules --> CLTools
    Wrapper --> CLTools
    CLTools --> Docs
    Docs --> CI
    CoreLib --> PyAPI
    PyAPI --> CI
    BuildSys --> CI
    BuildSys --> Docs
    CI -->|builds/tests| CoreLib
    CI -->|builds/tests| PyAPI
    CI -->|builds/tests| CLTools
```

This diagram shows the main subsystems and their dependencies. The build system orchestrates configuration, compilation, and quality checks. The core library implements simulation logic and APIs. Modules extend the core with additional features. Command-line tools and the Python interface provide user-facing utilities. Documentation and CI systems ensure quality and usability.

Sources: [configure:1-78](), [configure.ac:1-120](), [src/lib/Makefile:1-35](), [README.md:61-109]()

## Main Architectural Components

PLUMED is organized into several key systems:

| System                | Description                                                                                 | Main Code Entities / Files                |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Build & Quality       | Configuration, compilation, code quality checks                                             | `configure`, `configure.ac`, `Makefile`   |
| Core Library          | Main simulation logic, action framework, collective variables, biasing methods              | `src/lib/`, `src/core/`, `src/tools/`     |
| Modules               | Extensions for enhanced sampling, analysis, and specialized features                        | `src/*/` (e.g., `src/bias/`, `src/colvar/`) |
| External Interfaces   | APIs for C, C++, Fortran, Python; integration with MD codes                                 | `src/wrapper/Plumed.h`, `python/`         |
| Command-Line Tools    | User-facing utilities for analysis, patching, and more                                      | `src/cltools/`, `src/main/`               |
| Documentation         | Automated extraction and generation of user/developer documentation                         | `user-doc/`, `developer-doc/`, `Doxyfile` |
| CI & Packaging        | Continuous integration, testing, and packaging for distribution                            | `.github/`, `macports/`, `docker/`        |

### Bridging System Names to Code Entities

**Diagram: Core Library, Modules, and Interface Entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "PlumedMain(src/core/PlumedMain.h)" --> "Action(src/core/Action.h)"
    "Action(src/core/Action.h)" --> "Modules(src/bias/, src/colvar/, ...)"
    "PlumedMain(src/core/PlumedMain.h)" --> "TypesafePtr(src/core/TypesafePtr.h)"
    "Plumed.h(src/wrapper/Plumed.h)" --> "PlumedMain(src/core/PlumedMain.h)"
    "MDCode(GROMACS, LAMMPS, ...)" --> "Plumed.h(src/wrapper/Plumed.h)"
    "Modules(src/bias/, ...)" --> "Plumed.h(src/wrapper/Plumed.h)"
```

Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.h:1-100](), [src/core/Action.h:1-100](), [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:1-200]()

### Interface Layer

The main entry point for MD engines is the C/C++/Fortran interface in `src/wrapper/Plumed.h`. This interface provides the `cmd` function for communication, and is designed to be language-agnostic.

**Diagram: Interface Layer Code Entities**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "plumed" {
        +cmd(const char* key, const void* val)
        +finalize()
    }
    class "PLMD::Plumed" {
        +cmd(std::string_view key, const T& val)
        +finalize()
    }
    class "PLUMED_F_CMD" {
        +PLUMED_F_CMD(p, key, val)
        +PLUMED_F_FINALIZE(p)
    }
    "plumed" -- "PLMD::Plumed" : C++ Interface
    "plumed" -- "PLUMED_F_CMD" : Fortran Interface
```

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:62-78](), [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:226-262]()

### Core Engine: PlumedMain

The `PlumedMain` class is the central orchestrator. It receives commands from the interface, manages the lifecycle of actions, and coordinates data flow.

**Diagram: PlumedMain and Action Execution**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "cmd()" --> "PlumedMain"
    "PlumedMain" --> "parseCommand()"
    "PlumedMain" --> "executeActions()"
    "PlumedMain" --> "updateActions()"
    "PlumedMain" --> "ActionSet"
    "ActionSet" --> "Action1"
    "ActionSet" --> "Action2"
    "ActionSet" --> "ActionN"
```

Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-627](), [src/core/PlumedMain.h:81-86]()

### Action Framework

Actions are the modular units of computation in PLUMED. The base class is `Action`, with specialized subclasses for atomistic operations, collective variables, biases, and analysis.

**Diagram: Action Class Hierarchy**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "Action" {
        +prepare()
        +calculate()
        +apply()
        +update()
    }
    class "ActionAtomistic" {
        +requestAtoms()
        +retrieveAtoms()
    }
    class "ActionWithValue" {
        +setValue()
        +getValue()
    }
    class "ActionPilot" {
        +getStride()
    }
    class "Colvar"
    class "Bias"
    Action <|-- ActionAtomistic
    Action <|-- ActionWithValue
    Action <|-- ActionPilot
    ActionAtomistic <|-- Colvar
    ActionWithValue <|-- Bias
```

Sources: [src/core/Action.h:30-47](), [src/core/ActionAtomistic.h:30-42]()

Key action types:
- **Colvar**: Compute collective variables
- **Bias**: Apply biasing forces
- **Analysis**: Record/process simulation data


## Integration with MD Engines

PLUMED is typically loaded as a shared library or linked at build time with an MD engine. The main integration point is the `cmd` function in `src/wrapper/Plumed.h`, which is called by the MD engine to exchange data and trigger calculations.

**Diagram: MD Engine ↔ PLUMED Data Flow**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "MDCode" as "MD Engine"
    participant "Plumed.h" as "PLUMED Interface"
    participant "PlumedMain" as "PlumedMain"
    participant "Action" as "Actions"
    "MDCode"->>"Plumed.h": cmd("setPositions", positions)
    "Plumed.h"->>"PlumedMain": setPositions(positions)
    "PlumedMain"->>"Action": share positions
    "MDCode"->>"Plumed.h": cmd("calc")
    "Plumed.h"->>"PlumedMain": calc()
    "PlumedMain"->>"Action": calculate()
    "Action"->>"PlumedMain": return forces
    "PlumedMain"->>"Plumed.h": return forces
    "Plumed.h"->>"MDCode": return forces
```

Typical commands:
- `setPositions`: Provide atomic positions
- `setBox`: Set simulation box
- `setForces`: Provide forces
- `calc`: Calculate CVs and biases
- `update`: Update state

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:105-109](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:342-423]()

## Command-Line Tools

PLUMED provides several command-line tools for trajectory analysis, free-energy surface reconstruction, and other utilities. These tools reuse the core library and action framework.

**Diagram: Command-Line Tools and Core Library**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "driver(src/cltools/driver.cpp)" --> "CLToolMain(src/core/CLToolMain.cpp)"
    "sum_hills(src/cltools/sum_hills.cpp)" --> "CLToolMain(src/core/CLToolMain.cpp)"
    "pesmd(src/cltools/pesmd.cpp)" --> "CLToolMain(src/core/CLToolMain.cpp)"
    "CLToolMain(src/core/CLToolMain.cpp)" --> "PlumedMain(src/core/PlumedMain.cpp)"
    "PlumedMain(src/core/PlumedMain.cpp)" --> "Actions(src/core/Action.cpp)"
```

These tools allow users to run PLUMED analyses without an MD engine.

Sources: [src/core/CLToolMain.cpp:40-107](), [src/cltools/driver.cpp:1-100]()

## Build, Configuration, and Quality System

PLUMED uses a GNU Autoconf-based build system, with modular Makefiles and integrated code quality checks.

**Diagram: Build and Quality System Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "configure.ac" --> "configure"
    "configure" --> "Makefile.conf"
    "Makefile.conf" --> "Makefile"
    "Makefile" --> "src/lib/Makefile"
    "Makefile" --> "src/maketools/plumedcheck"
    "Makefile" --> "src/maketools/codecheck"
    "Makefile" --> "src/astyle.sh"
    "Makefile" --> "src/"
```

Key features:
- Modular configuration via `configure.ac` and `Makefile.conf`
- Optional modules can be enabled/disabled at configure time
- Code quality enforced by `plumedcheck`, `codecheck`, and `astyle`
- Cross-platform support and customizable installation layout

Sources: [configure:1-78](), [configure.ac:1-120](), [Makefile:1-100](), [src/lib/Makefile:1-100](), [src/maketools/plumedcheck:1-200](), [src/maketools/codecheck:1-100]()

## Version History (Selected Highlights)

| Version | Notable Features and Changes |
|---------|-----------------------------|
| 2.7     | OPES module, Funnel module, FISST module, improved Python interface |
| 2.8     | Typesafe C/C++/Fortran interfaces, new SASA module, improved error reporting |
| 2.9     | PyTorch module, MembraneFusion module, SANS CV, improved thread safety |
| 2.10+   | C++17 required, flexible data passing, Python CV plugin, CUDA plugin (planned) |

For detailed changes, see the `CHANGES/` directory.

Sources: [CHANGES/v2.7.md:1-110](), [CHANGES/v2.8.md:1-131](), [CHANGES/v2.9.md:1-85](), [CHANGES/v2.10.md:1-60]()

## Conclusion

PLUMED provides a flexible and powerful framework for enhancing molecular dynamics simulations. Its modular architecture allows for easy extension and integration with various MD engines, while its comprehensive set of actions enables a wide range of enhanced sampling and analysis methods.

For more detailed information about specific components, please refer to the respective wiki pages:
- For details on the core architecture, see [Core Architecture](#2)
- For information about the action framework, see [Action Framework](#2.3)
- For enhanced sampling methods, see [Enhanced Sampling Methods](#3)

This page describes the main architectural layers and design patterns of PLUMED, focusing on the relationships between the build system, core library, modules, and interfaces. For details on enhanced sampling algorithms, see [Enhanced Sampling Methods](3). For integrative modeling, see [Integrative Modeling](4).

## High-Level System Overview

PLUMED is organized into several key architectural layers:

- **Build & Quality System**: Handles configuration, compilation, and code quality.
- **Core Library**: Implements the main simulation logic and APIs.
- **Modules**: Extend the core with additional features (e.g., biases, collective variables).
- **External Interfaces**: Allow MD engines and other tools to interact with PLUMED.
- **Command-Line Tools**: User-facing utilities for analysis and setup.
- **Documentation and CI**: Automated documentation and continuous integration.

### Diagram: PLUMED Core System Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Build&QualitySystem"
        BuildSys["configure, configure.ac, Makefile, plumedcheck"]
    end
    subgraph "CoreLibrary"
        CoreLib["libplumedKernel, PlumedMain, Actions"]
        Wrapper["Plumed.h (C/C++/Fortran API)"]
    end
    subgraph "Modules"
        Modules["src/*/ (Bias, Colvar, Function, etc.)"]
    end
    subgraph "CommandLineTools"
        CLTools["driver, sum_hills, pesmd, etc."]
    end
    subgraph "Documentation"
        Docs["user-doc/, developer-doc/, Doxygen"]
    end
    subgraph "CI&Packaging"
        CI[".github/, Conda, Docker, MacPorts"]
    end
    subgraph "PythonInterface"
        PyAPI["python/plumed.pyx, cplumed.pxd"]
    end

    BuildSys --> CoreLib
    CoreLib --> Wrapper
    CoreLib --> Modules
    Modules --> CLTools
    Wrapper --> CLTools
    CLTools --> Docs
    Docs --> CI
    CoreLib --> PyAPI
    PyAPI --> CI
    BuildSys --> CI
    BuildSys --> Docs
    CI --> CoreLib
    CI --> PyAPI
    CI --> CLTools
```

**Mapping to Code Entities:**

| System Layer         | Key Code Entities / Files                                  |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Build & Quality      | `configure`, `configure.ac`, `Makefile`, `plumedcheck`    |
| Core Library         | `src/core/PlumedMain.cpp`, `src/core/Action.cpp`          |
| Modules              | `src/bias/`, `src/colvar/`, etc.                          |
| External Interface   | `src/wrapper/Plumed.h`                                    |
| Command-Line Tools   | `src/cltools/driver.cpp`, etc.                            |
| Documentation        | `user-doc/`, `developer-doc/`, `Doxygen`                  |
| CI & Packaging       | `.github/`, `macports/`, `docker/`                        |
| Python Interface     | `python/plumed.pyx`, `python/cplumed.pxd`                 |

Sources: [configure](), [configure.ac](), [src/wrapper/Plumed.h](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp](), [src/core/Action.cpp](), [src/lib/Makefile](), [src/maketools/plumedcheck]()

## Core Architectural Layers and Relationships

PLUMED's architecture is layered to separate concerns and enable extensibility. The following diagram maps the main system names to code entities.

### Diagram: Layered Architecture and Code Entities

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "ExternalMDCode"
        MDCode["MD Codes (GROMACS, LAMMPS, etc.)"]
    end
    subgraph "ExternalInterface"
        PlumedH["Plumed.h"]
    end
    subgraph "CoreLibrary"
        PlumedMain["PlumedMain"]
        TypesafePtr["TypesafePtr"]
        ActionSet["ActionSet"]
    end
    subgraph "Modules"
        Bias["src/bias/"]
        Colvar["src/colvar/"]
        Function["src/function/"]
        ToolsMod["src/tools/"]
    end

    MDCode --> PlumedH
    PlumedH --> PlumedMain
    PlumedMain --> TypesafePtr
    PlumedMain --> ActionSet
    ActionSet --> Bias
    ActionSet --> Colvar
    ActionSet --> Function
    ActionSet --> ToolsMod
```

**Key Code Entities:**

| Layer              | Code Entity / File                  | Description                                 |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| External Interface | `src/wrapper/Plumed.h`              | C/C++/Fortran API for MD code integration   |
| Core Library       | `src/core/PlumedMain.cpp`           | Main orchestrator, command dispatcher       |
| Core Library       | `src/tools/TypesafePtr.h`           | Type-safe data exchange                     |
| Core Library       | `src/core/ActionSet.h`              | Manages registered actions                  |
| Modules            | `src/bias/`, `src/colvar/`, etc.    | Extend core with new features               |

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp](), [src/core/ActionSet.h](), [src/tools/TypesafePtr.h]()

## Core Library: Main Orchestrator and Action System

### PlumedMain and ActionSet

The `PlumedMain` class is the central orchestrator of PLUMED. It receives commands from the interface, manages the simulation state, and coordinates the execution of actions.

#### Diagram: PlumedMain and ActionSet Class Relationships

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "PlumedMain" {
        +Communicator comm
        +ActionSet actionSet
        +cmd(word, val)
        +init()
        +readInputFile(file)
        +prepareCalc()
        +performCalc()
        +update()
    }
    class "ActionSet" {
        +std::vector<Action*> actions
        +selectWithLabel()
        +selectLatest()
        +select()
    }
    class "Action" {
        <<abstract>>
    }
    PlumedMain --> ActionSet : "manages"
    ActionSet --> Action : "contains"
```

- `PlumedMain` handles the main simulation loop and command dispatch.
- `ActionSet` manages all registered actions (instances of `Action` and its subclasses).
- Actions are modular units of computation (e.g., CVs, biases, analysis).

Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:285-304](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-636](), [src/core/PlumedMain.h:81-205](), [src/core/ActionSet.h]()

### Simulation Step and Command Flow

PLUMED operates by receiving a sequence of commands from the MD engine at each simulation step. The `cmd()` method in `PlumedMain` is the main entry point for these commands.

#### Diagram: Simulation Step Command Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "MD Engine"
    participant "PlumedMain::cmd"
    participant "ActionSet"
    participant "Action"
    "MD Engine"->>"PlumedMain::cmd": setStep(step)
    "MD Engine"->>"PlumedMain::cmd": setPositions(pos)
    "MD Engine"->>"PlumedMain::cmd": setBox(box)
    "MD Engine"->>"PlumedMain::cmd": setForces(forces)
    "MD Engine"->>"PlumedMain::cmd": setEnergy(energy)
    "PlumedMain::cmd"->>"ActionSet": prepareDependencies()
    "ActionSet"->>"Action": prepare()
    "PlumedMain::cmd"->>"ActionSet": shareData()
    "PlumedMain::cmd"->>"ActionSet": prepareCalc()
    "ActionSet"->>"Action": prepareCalc()
    "PlumedMain::cmd"->>"ActionSet": performCalc()
    "ActionSet"->>"Action": calculate()
    "PlumedMain::cmd"->>"ActionSet": update()
    "ActionSet"->>"Action": update()
    "PlumedMain::cmd"->>"MD Engine": Return forces, energy
```

- Each command (e.g., `setStep`, `setPositions`) is handled by `PlumedMain::cmd`.
- Actions are executed in a dependency-aware order.
- Results (forces, energies) are returned to the MD engine.

Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-636](), [src/core/PlumedMain.h:205-285]()

## Action Framework and Extensibility

PLUMED's functionality is implemented through a modular action system. Each action is a C++ class derived from a common base and is registered using a factory pattern.

### Diagram: Action Class Hierarchy and Registration

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "Action" {
        <<abstract>>
    }
    class "ActionAtomistic" {
        // Atom-based actions
    }
    class "ActionWithValue" {
        // Produces values
    }
    class "ActionWithArguments" {
        // Depends on other actions
    }
    class "ActionRegister" {
        +registerAction()
    }
    ActionRegister ..> Action : "creates"
    Action <|-- ActionAtomistic
    Action <|-- ActionWithValue
    Action <|-- ActionWithArguments
```

- `ActionRegister` implements the factory pattern for dynamic action creation.
- Actions are organized in a class hierarchy for extensibility.
- New actions can be added as modules without modifying the core.

Sources: [src/core/ActionRegister.h:1-100](), [src/core/ActionRegister.cpp:1-50](), [src/core/Action.h:1-200](), [src/core/ActionAtomistic.h:1-100](), [src/core/ActionAtomistic.cpp:1-100]()

### Keyword and Input Management

Actions are configured via a keyword system, which is managed by the `Keywords` class. This system supports documentation, parsing, and validation of input parameters.

#### Diagram: Action and Keywords Relationship

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "Keywords" {
        +add(keyword, doc)
        +addFlag(keyword, doc, default)
        +exists(keyword)
        +getKeywords()
    }
    class "Action" {
        +Keywords keywords
        +registerKeywords(Keywords&)
        +parseFlag(key, val)
        +parseVector(key, val)
    }
    Action --> Keywords : "uses"
```

- Keywords can be compulsory, optional, or flags.
- Supports scalar, vector, and atom index values.

Sources: [src/tools/Keywords.cpp:1-100](), [src/tools/Keywords.cpp:100-200]()

## Data Flow and Type Safety

PLUMED uses a type-safe pointer system (`TypesafePtr`) to exchange data between the interface, core, and actions. This ensures that data passed (such as positions, forces, energies) is checked for type and shape at runtime.

### Diagram: Data Flow and TypesafePtr

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    MDPositions["Atomic Positions"] --> PlumedMain
    MDBox["Box Dimensions"] --> PlumedMain
    PlumedMain --> CVs["Collective Variables (Actions)"]
    CVs --> BiasForces["Bias Forces (Actions)"]
    BiasForces --> PlumedMain
    PlumedMain --> MDForces["Forces"]
    PlumedMain --> MDEnergy["Energy"]
    PlumedMain -.-> TypesafePtr["TypesafePtr"]
    CVs -.-> TypesafePtr
    BiasForces -.-> TypesafePtr
```

- All data passed through the interface and between actions uses `TypesafePtr` for runtime type checking.
- This mechanism is implemented in both the C++ and C interfaces.

Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-636](), [src/core/ActionAtomistic.cpp:1-200](), [src/tools/TypesafePtr.h]()

## Build and Configuration System

PLUMED's build system is based on Autoconf and Makefiles, supporting modular compilation, code quality checks, and flexible installation.

### Diagram: Build System Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Configure["configure (Autoconf)"] --> MakefileConf["Makefile.conf (generated)"]
    MakefileConf --> MakeSrc["src/Makefile"]
    MakeSrc --> MakeLib["src/lib/Makefile"]
    MakeLib --> Modules["src/*/ (modules)"]
    MakeLib --> Wrapper["src/wrapper/Plumed.h"]
    MakeLib --> Kernel["libplumedKernel"]
```

- `configure` and `configure.ac` detect system capabilities and generate `Makefile.conf`.
- Makefiles in `src/` and `src/lib/` orchestrate compilation of the core, modules, and wrapper.
- Code quality tools (e.g., `plumedcheck`) are integrated into the build.

Sources: [configure:1-500](), [configure.ac:1-200](), [src/lib/Makefile:1-100](), [Makefile:1-50](), [src/maketools/plumedcheck]()

## Exception and Error Handling

PLUMED uses C++ exceptions for error handling, with translation layers in the interface to ensure robust error reporting across C, C++, and Fortran.

### Diagram: Exception Propagation and Handling

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MDCode["MD Engine"] --> PlumedH["Plumed.h"]
    PlumedH --> PlumedMain["PlumedMain"]
    PlumedMain --> Exception["Exception (std::exception, ExceptionError, etc.)"]
    Exception --> PlumedH
    PlumedH --> MDCode
```

- Exceptions thrown in `PlumedMain` are caught and translated by the interface layer.
- The interface returns error codes or messages to the MD engine, preventing crashes.

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:278-317](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:74-242]()

## Reference Counting and Object Lifetime

PLUMED manages the lifetime of its core objects using reference counting, allowing safe sharing of instances across interfaces and threads.

### Diagram: Reference Counting in Object Lifecycle

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Create["plumed_create()"] --> RefCounter["Reference Counter"]
    CreateReference["plumed_create_reference()"] --> RefCounter
    Finalize["plumed_finalize()"] --> RefCounter
    RefCounter -->|"when zero"| Destroy["Destroy PlumedMain"]
```

- Each `plumed_create` or `plumed_create_reference` increments the counter.
- `plumed_finalize` decrements it.
- When the counter reaches zero, the object is destroyed.

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:211-223](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:285-304]()

## Utility Layer

The utility layer provides reusable components for mathematical operations, periodic boundary conditions, file I/O, and parsing.

### Diagram: Utility Layer Usage

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PlumedMain["PlumedMain"] --> Math["tools/Vector, tools/Tensor"]
    PlumedMain --> PBC["tools/Pbc"]
    PlumedMain --> FileIO["tools/IFile, tools/OFile"]
    PlumedMain --> Parser["tools/Tools"]
    Actions["Actions"] --> Math
    Actions --> PBC
    Actions --> FileIO
```

- Utilities are used by both the core and actions for common tasks.

Sources: [src/tools/Tools.cpp:1-200](), [src/tools/Pbc.cpp:1-200](), [src/tools/Tools.h:1-200]()

## Summary

The PLUMED core architecture is designed for flexibility, extensibility, and robustness. The separation between the interface layer and the implementation allows PLUMED to work with various MD engines while maintaining a consistent internal structure. The modular action system enables easy extension with new functionality, and the calculation lifecycle ensures proper handling of dependencies and data flow.

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h]()/[src/core/PlumedMain.cpp]()/[src/core/Action.h]()/[src/core/ActionRegister.h]()

# Build System

The PLUMED build system configures, compiles, and installs the PLUMED software. It is designed for portability, modularity, and integration with a variety of molecular dynamics (MD) engines. The system is based on GNU Autoconf for configuration and GNU Make for building, and includes code quality checks and installation layout logic.

For an overview of the overall architecture, see [Core Architecture](2).

---

## High-Level Build System Flow

The build system consists of several key stages: configuration, build, and output generation. The following diagram maps the main code entities involved in each stage.

**Diagram: Build System Flow and Code Entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Configuration"
        "configure.ac"["configure.ac"] -->|"autoconf"| "configure"["configure (script)"]
        "configure" -->|"generates"| "Makefile.conf"
        "Makefile.conf.in"["Makefile.conf.in"] -->|"template"| "Makefile.conf"
    end

    subgraph "Build"
        "Makefile.conf" -->|"included by"| "Makefile"
        "Makefile" -->|"calls"| "src/Makefile"
        "src/Makefile" -->|"calls"| "src/lib/Makefile"
    end

    subgraph "Output"
        "src/lib/Makefile" -->|"produces"| "libplumedKernel.so"
        "src/lib/Makefile" -->|"produces"| "libplumed.so"
        "src/lib/Makefile" -->|"produces"| "libplumedWrapper.a"
        "src/lib/Makefile" -->|"produces"| "plumed (executable)"
    end
```

**Key Code Entities:**
- `configure.ac`, `configure`, `Makefile.conf.in`, `Makefile.conf`
- `Makefile`, `src/Makefile`, `src/lib/Makefile`
- Output artifacts: `libplumedKernel.so`, `libplumed.so`, `libplumedWrapper.a`, `plumed`

Sources: [configure.ac:1-146](), [Makefile:1-153](), [src/Makefile:1-72](), [src/lib/Makefile:1-100]()

## Configuration Process

The configuration process is handled by the `configure` script, which is generated from `configure.ac` using Autoconf. This script detects system features, compiler capabilities, and available libraries, and sets up the build environment according to user-specified options.

### Running the Configure Script

Basic usage:

```bash
./configure [options]
```

The script supports a wide range of options for customizing the build. The most important options are summarized below.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--prefix=DIR` | Install files in DIR (default: `/usr/local`) |
| `--enable-modules=LIST` | Enable/disable modules (see below) |
| `--enable-mpi` | Enable MPI support |
| `--enable-debug` | Enable debugging |
| `--enable-shared` | Build shared libraries (default: yes) |
| `--enable-static-archive` | Build static library archive (default: yes) |
| `--enable-cxx=LEVEL` | Set C++ standard (17, 20, or 23) |
| `--disable-doc` | Disable documentation generation |
| `--disable-libsearch` | Disable automatic library detection |

Sources: [configure.ac:195-327](), [configure:1-500]()

---

### Module Management

PLUMED is organized into modules, which can be enabled or disabled at configuration time. Modules are classified as `always`, `default-on`, or `default-off`. The `--enable-modules` option controls which modules are included.

**Diagram: Module Enable/Disable Logic**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "configure.ac"["configure.ac"] -->|"--enable-modules=all"| "Enable all modules"
    "configure.ac" -->|"--enable-modules=none"| "Disable all optional modules"
    "configure.ac" -->|"--enable-modules=reset"| "Reset to default"
    "configure.ac" -->|"--enable-modules=+modA:-modB"| "Enable/disable specific modules"

    subgraph "Module Types"
        "always"["always"]
        "default-on"["default-on"]
        "default-off"["default-off"]
    end
```

**Examples:**
```bash
./configure --enable-modules=all
./configure --enable-modules=none
./configure --enable-modules=+crystallization:-bias
```

Sources: [configure.ac:198-253]()

## Build Process

After configuration, the build process is managed by GNU Make. The main entry points are the top-level `Makefile`, `src/Makefile`, and `src/lib/Makefile`. These Makefiles coordinate the compilation of libraries, executables, and scripts.

### Build Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `make` | Build PLUMED libraries and executables |
| `make install` | Install PLUMED to the specified prefix |
| `make clean` | Remove build artifacts |
| `make distclean` | Remove all build and configuration files |
| `make check` | Run tests (non-installed PLUMED) |
| `make installcheck` | Run tests (installed PLUMED) |

Sources: [Makefile:16-77](), [src/Makefile:1-72](), [src/lib/Makefile:1-100]()

---

### Build Outputs and Artifacts

PLUMED produces several libraries and executables to support different integration and usage scenarios.

**Diagram: Build Outputs and Their Relationships**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Libraries"
        "libplumedKernel.so"["libplumedKernel.so/dylib (core)"]
        "libplumed.so"["libplumed.so/dylib (complete)"]
        "libplumedWrapper.a"["libplumedWrapper.a (static wrapper)"]
    end

    subgraph "Executables"
        "plumed"["plumed (main executable)"]
        "plumed-static"["plumed-static (static)"]
        "plumed-runtime"["plumed-runtime (runtime loading)"]
    end

    "libplumedKernel.so" -->|"linked by"| "libplumed.so"
    "libplumedKernel.so" -->|"linked by"| "plumed-static"
    "libplumed.so" -->|"linked by"| "plumed"
    "libplumedWrapper.a" -->|"runtime loading"| "libplumedKernel.so"
    "plumed-runtime" -->|"loads at runtime"| "libplumedKernel.so"
```

Sources: [src/lib/Makefile:73-99]()

## Integration with MD Engines

PLUMED supports multiple integration methods with molecular dynamics (MD) engines. The build system produces different artifacts to support these methods.

**Diagram: Integration Methods and Code Artifacts**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "IntegrationMethods"
        "RuntimeLoading"["Runtime Loading"]
        "DynamicLinking"["Dynamic Linking"]
        "StaticLinking"["Static Linking"]
    end

    subgraph "PLUMEDLibraries"
        "libplumedKernel.so"["libplumedKernel.so/dylib"]
        "libplumed.so"["libplumed.so/dylib"]
        "libplumedWrapper.a"["libplumedWrapper.a"]
    end

    subgraph "MDEngine"
        "PatchedMDCode"["Patched MD Code"]
    end

    "RuntimeLoading" -->|"uses"| "libplumedWrapper.a"
    "libplumedWrapper.a" -->|"loads"| "libplumedKernel.so"
    "DynamicLinking" -->|"links against"| "libplumed.so"
    "StaticLinking" -->|"embeds"| "libplumedWrapper.a"
    "PatchedMDCode" -->|"calls"| "RuntimeLoading"
    "PatchedMDCode" -->|"calls"| "DynamicLinking"
    "PatchedMDCode" -->|"contains"| "StaticLinking"
```

- **Runtime Loading**: MD code statically links `libplumedWrapper.a` and loads `libplumedKernel.so` at runtime.
- **Dynamic Linking**: MD code links directly against `libplumed.so`.
- **Static Linking**: PLUMED source or objects are compiled directly into the MD code.

Sources: [src/lib/Makefile:434-515]()

## Dependency Management

PLUMED supports a range of optional dependencies, which can be enabled or disabled at configuration time. The build system detects and configures these dependencies as needed.

| Dependency | Configure Option | Purpose |
|------------|-----------------|---------|
| LAPACK/BLAS | `--enable-external-lapack/blas` | Linear algebra |
| MPI | `--enable-mpi` | Parallel execution |
| FFTW | `--enable-fftw` | Fast Fourier Transforms |
| GSL | `--enable-gsl` | Advanced math functions |
| Python | `--enable-python` | Python interface |
| OpenMP | `--enable-openmp` | Shared-memory parallelism |
| zlib | `--enable-zlib` | Compression support |

The `--disable-libsearch` option disables automatic library detection, requiring explicit library paths.

Sources: [configure.ac:514-836]()

## Installation

The installation process copies built files to their final locations as specified by the configuration.

### Installation Paths

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `prefix` | `/usr/local` | Base installation directory |
| `bindir` | `${prefix}/bin` | Executables directory |
| `libdir` | `${prefix}/lib` | Libraries directory |
| `includedir` | `${prefix}/include` | Header files directory |
| `htmldir` | `${datarootdir}/doc/${PACKAGE_TARNAME}` | Documentation directory |

Sources: [Makefile.conf.in:19-50](), [configure.ac:807-825]()

### Installation Steps

The `make install` target performs the following:

1. Creates required directories
2. Installs libraries (`libplumed.so`, `libplumedKernel.so`, `libplumedWrapper.a`)
3. Installs executables (`plumed`, `plumed-patch`, etc.)
4. Installs header files
5. Installs documentation and examples
6. Installs additional tools and scripts

Sources: [src/lib/Makefile:212-386]()

## Distribution and Packaging

PLUMED supports packaging for multiple platforms and package managers.

- **MacPorts**: Templates in `macports/` for MacPorts packaging (`Portfile.in`, `PortfilePython.in`)
- **Conda**: Recipes in `conda/` for Conda packages (`plumed/meta.yaml`, `plumed/build.sh`, `py-plumed/`)
- **Docker**: Dockerfiles in `docker/` for various Linux distributions

Sources: [macports/Portfile.in:1-122](), [conda/plumed/meta.yaml:1-65](), [docker/Makefile:1-24]()

PLUMED uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration (CI) across multiple platforms. The CI system builds, tests, and checks code quality for all supported configurations.


The CI system performs:
- Compilation with different compilers and options
- Unit and regression tests
- Code style and formatting checks
- Packaging tests

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-37](), [.github/workflows/macWF.yml:1-99](), [.github/workflows/codecheckWF.yml:1-18]()

The build system integrates several tools for code quality and static analysis.

## Conclusion

The PLUMED build system provides a flexible framework for compiling, installing, and distributing the software. It supports various integration methods with MD engines, platform-specific optimizations, and optional dependencies. By understanding the build system, users can customize PLUMED to their specific needs and environments.

This page documents the external interfaces of PLUMED, focusing on the C, C++, Fortran, and Python APIs that allow molecular dynamics (MD) codes and user scripts to interact with the PLUMED core. The interface is designed for stability, language interoperability, and minimal integration effort for host codes.

## System Context and Interface Role

PLUMED's interface layer is the primary entry point for external MD engines and user tools. It provides a stable API for data exchange and command invocation, abstracting the internal implementation details of the PLUMED core.

### Diagram: High-Level System Integration

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "MDCode[\"MD Engine (e.g. GROMACS, LAMMPS)\"]" -->|"\"plumed_cmd / PLMD::Plumed::cmd / PLUMED_F_CMD\""| "Plumed_h[\"src/wrapper/Plumed.h\"]"
    "Plumed_h" -->|"\"cmd()\""| "PlumedMain[\"PLMD::PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)\"]"
    "PlumedMain" -->|"\"ActionSet, CVs, Modules\""| "Actions[\"Action Framework\"]"
    "Python[\"python/plumed.pyx\"]" -->|"\"Plumed class, cmd()\""| "Plumed_h"
```
Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:35-47](), [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:80-92](), [python/plumed.pyx:69-287]()

**Key interface goals:**
- Language compatibility (C, C++, Fortran, Python)
- Binary and API stability
- Minimal dependencies for host codes
- Thread safety and reference counting
- Robust error and exception handling


## Interface Structure and Code Entities

The PLUMED interface is implemented as a thin wrapper object that holds a pointer to the actual core implementation. This design enables language bindings and binary compatibility.

- **C:** `struct plumed` (contains a `void*` pointer)
- **C++:** `PLMD::Plumed` class (wraps `struct plumed`)
- **Fortran:** `CHARACTER(LEN=32)` string (stores pointer as text)
- **Python:** `Plumed` class in `python/plumed.pyx` (wraps C interface)

### Diagram: Interface Object Mapping to Code Entities

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "plumed (struct)" {
        void* p
    }
    class "PLMD::Plumed" {
        +cmd(key, val)
        +finalize()
        +valid() bool
        +dlopen(path)
        +toFortran(char*)
        +incref()
        +decref()
    }
    class "PLMD::PlumedMain" {
        -initialized: bool
        -step: long long int
        -active: bool
        +cmd(key, val)
        +init()
        +prepareCalc()
        +performCalc()
        -actionSet: ActionSet
    }
    class "python.plumed.PyPlumed" as PyPlumed {
        +cmd(key, val)
        +finalize()
        +__enter__/__exit__
    }
    "plumed" --> "PLMD::PlumedMain" : "p points to"
    "PLMD::Plumed" --> "plumed" : "wraps"
    "PyPlumed" --> "plumed" : "wraps"
```
Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:797-808](), [src/core/PlumedMain.h:81-534](), [python/plumed.pyx:69-287]()


## Command Communication Flow

The main communication mechanism is the `cmd` method (or `plumed_cmd` in C/Fortran), which takes a command string and a value pointer. This method is the entry point for all data exchange and control between the MD code and PLUMED.

### Diagram: Command Flow from MD Code to PLUMED Core

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "MD" as "MD Engine"
    participant "Wrapper" as "plumed_cmd / PLMD::Plumed::cmd"
    participant "PlumedMain" as "PLMD::PlumedMain::cmd"
    participant "Actions" as "ActionSet"

    "MD"->>"Wrapper": "plumed_cmd(\"init\", NULL)"
    "Wrapper"->>"PlumedMain": "cmd(\"init\", NULL)"
    "PlumedMain"->>"PlumedMain": "initialize()"

    "MD"->>"Wrapper": "plumed_cmd(\"setPositions\", positions)"
    "Wrapper"->>"PlumedMain": "cmd(\"setPositions\", positions)"
    "PlumedMain"->>"PlumedMain": "setInputValue()"

    "MD"->>"Wrapper": "plumed_cmd(\"calc\", NULL)"
    "Wrapper"->>"PlumedMain": "cmd(\"calc\", NULL)"
    "PlumedMain"->>"Actions": "calculate()"
    "Actions"->>"PlumedMain": "return forces"

    "MD"->>"Wrapper": "plumed_cmd(\"getBias\", &energy)"
    "Wrapper"->>"PlumedMain": "cmd(\"getBias\", &energy)"
    "PlumedMain"->>"Wrapper": "return bias energy"
    "Wrapper"->>"MD": "store energy value"
```
Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-442](), [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:104-109]()


## Typesafe Interface and Data Validation

Starting with PLUMED 2.8, the interface performs runtime type checking to ensure safe data exchange. This includes:

- Verifying value types (integer, float, pointer, etc.)
- Checking array sizes and shapes
- Enabling or disabling type checks via environment variables

### Diagram: Typesafe Command Dispatch

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "CXX_cmd[\"PLMD::Plumed::cmd(key, value)\"]" --> "CXX_TypeCheck[\"C++ type checking (runtime)\"]"
    "C_cmd[\"plumed_cmd(p, key, value)\"]" --> "C_TypeCheck[\"C11 _Generic type checking\"]"
    "F_cmd[\"PLUMED_F_CMD(p, key, value)\"]" --> "NoTypeCheck[\"No runtime type check\"]"
    "CXX_TypeCheck" --> "PlumedMain_cmd[\"PLMD::PlumedMain::cmd\"]"
    "C_TypeCheck" --> "PlumedMain_cmd"
    "NoTypeCheck" --> "PlumedMain_cmd"
```
Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:317-347](), [src/tools/TypesafePtr.h:108-198]()


## Object Lifecycle and Reference Counting

The PLUMED interface uses explicit object lifecycle management, with reference counting to support safe usage in multi-language and multi-threaded contexts.

### Diagram: PLUMED Object Lifecycle

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> "Created": "plumed_create()"
    "Created" --> "Initialized": "plumed_cmd(\"init\", NULL)"
    "Initialized" --> "Operating": "plumed_cmd / cmd calls"
    "Operating" --> "Finalized": "plumed_finalize()"
    "Finalized" --> [*]

    note right of "Created"
        Reference counter = 1
    end note

    note right of "Operating"
        Data exchange and calculations
    end note

    note right of "Finalized"
        Resources released when reference counter = 0
    end note
```
Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:111-141](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:293-303]()


## Command Processing Workflow

When an MD code calls the PLUMED interface, the command is processed through a series of layers, ultimately invoking the appropriate logic in the core.

### Diagram: Command Processing Path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "MDCode[\"MD Code\"]" -->|"\"plumed_cmd(p, key, val)\""| "Wrapper[\"src/wrapper/Plumed.h\"]"
    "Wrapper" -->|"\"cmd(key, val)\""| "PlumedMain[\"PLMD::PlumedMain::cmd\"]"
    "PlumedMain" --> "ParseCommand[\"Parse command string\"]"
    "ParseCommand" --> "SwitchCase[\"Switch on command ID\"]"
    "SwitchCase" --> "ExecuteAction[\"Execute action or data exchange\"]"
    "ExecuteAction" -->|"\"Results/Status\""| "Wrapper"
    "Wrapper" -->|"\"Return values\""| "MDCode"
```
Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-442](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:625-676]()


## Key Interface Commands

The PLUMED interface supports a set of standardized commands for initialization, data transfer, calculation, and result retrieval.

| Command Category | Example Commands | Description |
|------------------|------------------|-------------|
| Initialization   | `init`, `setRealPrecision`, `setNatoms` | Set up PLUMED before simulation |
| Data Input       | `setPositions`, `setForces`, `setBox`, `setMasses`, `setCharges` | Pass data from MD to PLUMED |
| Calculation      | `calc`, `prepareCalc`, `performCalc` | Trigger PLUMED calculations |
| Data Output      | `getBias`, `getForces` | Retrieve results from PLUMED |
| Configuration    | `setMDEngine`, `setTimestep`, `setKbT` | Configure PLUMED parameters |
| Utility          | `getApiVersion`, `isEnergyNeeded` | Query PLUMED status |

Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-901]()


## Data Exchange Between MD Codes and PLUMED

PLUMED exchanges simulation data with MD codes through the interface, including positions, forces, box dimensions, and energies.

### Diagram: Data Flow for Input and Output

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "MD_Positions[\"setPositions\"]" --> "PLUMED"
    "MD_Forces[\"setForces\"]" --> "PLUMED"
    "MD_Masses[\"setMasses\"]" --> "PLUMED"
    "MD_Charges[\"setCharges\"]" --> "PLUMED"
    "MD_Box[\"setBox\"]" --> "PLUMED"
    "MD_Energy[\"setEnergy\"]" --> "PLUMED"
    "PLUMED" --> "PLUMED_Calc[\"Calculate CVs, Bias, Actions\"]"
    "PLUMED_Calc" --> "PLUMED"
    "PLUMED" --> "MD_BiasForces[\"getForces\"]"
    "PLUMED" --> "MD_BiasEnergy[\"getBias\"]"
    "PLUMED" --> "MD_Virial[\"getVirial\"]"
```
Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:343-403](), [src/core/ActionAtomistic.cpp:444-500]()


## Error and Exception Handling

The PLUMED interface provides robust error handling at the language boundary. Exceptions thrown in the core are remapped or reported according to the calling language.

### Diagram: Error Handling and Exception Remapping

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "plumed_cmd_call[\"plumed_cmd call\"]" --> "TryCatch[\"try-catch in cmd()\"]"
    "TryCatch" -->|"\"Exception occurs\""| "ExceptionThrown[\"Exception thrown\"]"
    "ExceptionThrown" --> "ExceptionCaught[\"Exception caught at interface\"]"
    "ExceptionCaught" --> "CXX_Remap[\"C++: Remap and rethrow\"]"
    "ExceptionCaught" --> "C_Fortran_Handle[\"C/Fortran: Handle error, terminate or report\"]"
    "CXX_Remap" --> "MDCode[\"MD code receives exception\"]"
```
Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:278-316](), [src/core/PlumedMainInitializer.cpp:128-565]()


## Language-Specific Interfaces

PLUMED provides tailored interfaces for C, C++, Fortran, and Python. All interfaces are built on the same underlying object and command mechanism.

### Mapping of Interface Functions

| Language | Creation         | Command Invocation         | Finalization         | File(s) |
|----------|------------------|---------------------------|----------------------|---------|
| C        | `plumed_create()`| `plumed_cmd(p, key, val)` | `plumed_finalize(p)` | [src/wrapper/Plumed.h]() |
| C++      | `PLMD::Plumed()` | `cmd(key, val)`           | Destructor           | [src/wrapper/Plumed.h]() |
| Fortran  | `PLUMED_F_CREATE`| `PLUMED_F_CMD`            | `PLUMED_F_FINALIZE`  | [src/wrapper/Plumed.h]() |
| Python   | `Plumed()`       | `cmd(key, val)`           | `finalize()`         | [python/plumed.pyx]()    |

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:227-263](), [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:104-141](), [python/plumed.pyx:69-287]()


## Interface Version Evolution

The PLUMED interface is designed for backward compatibility, with new features added in recent versions:

| Version | Major Improvements |
|---------|-------------------|
| 2.5     | Rewritten wrappers, reference counting, improved exception handling |
| 2.8     | Runtime type checking, enhanced Fortran interface |
| 2.9     | Thread-safe reference counter, nested exception support, long integer support |

Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:348-424]()


## Using Multiple PLUMED Versions at Runtime

The interface supports loading different PLUMED kernel versions at runtime, allowing MD codes to select the desired version dynamically.

### Diagram: Runtime Kernel Selection

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "MDCode[\"MD Code\"]" -->|"\"plumed_create()\""| "Default[\"Default Version\"]"
    "MDCode" -->|"\"plumed_create_dlopen('libplumed_2.7.so')\""| "PLUMED27[\"PLUMED 2.7\"]"
    "MDCode" -->|"\"plumed_create_dlopen('libplumed_2.8.so')\""| "PLUMED28[\"PLUMED 2.8\"]"
    "MDCode" -->|"\"plumed_create_dlopen('libplumed_2.9.so')\""| "PLUMED29[\"PLUMED 2.9\"]"
```
Sources: [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:119-126](), [src/wrapper/Plumed.h:411-415]()


## Summary

The PLUMED interface provides a robust, language-agnostic way for MD engines to incorporate PLUMED functionality. Its design emphasizes compatibility across versions, clear error handling, and minimal dependency requirements for the MD code. Recent versions have added type safety and improved thread safety, making the interface more robust while maintaining the same overall structure.

The interface is centered around a simple object and the `cmd` method, providing a unified way to access all of PLUMED's functionality from different programming languages.

The Action Framework is the central architectural system in PLUMED for defining, registering, instantiating, and executing modular units of computation called "Actions". Actions are the primary mechanism for implementing collective variables (CVs), biases, analysis, and other operations in a simulation.

## System Overview

The Action Framework organizes the flow from user input to simulation logic through a set of core classes and data structures. Each Action corresponds to a line in the input file (typically `plumed.dat`), and is managed by a central registry and execution engine.

**Diagram: High-Level Action Framework Data Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "ActionFramework"
        AR["ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)"]
        AC["Action (src/core/Action.h) and subclasses"]
        AS["ActionSet (src/core/ActionSet.h)"]
        PMain["PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)"]
    end

    Input["Input File [plumed.dat]"] --> PMain
    PMain --> AR
    AR --> AC
    AC --> AS
    AS --> PMain
    PMain --> MD["MD Engine"]
```
Sources: [src/core/Action.h](), [src/core/ActionRegister.h](), [src/core/PlumedMain.h]()

This diagram shows the main code entities involved in the Action Framework and their relationships.

## Action Class Hierarchy

The Action Framework is structured as a class hierarchy, with the base class `Action` providing the core interface. Specialized subclasses add features for atomistic operations, value storage, argument parsing, and more.

**Diagram: Action Class Hierarchy and Key Methods**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "Action (src/core/Action.h)" {
        +name: string
        +label: string
        +plumed: PlumedMain&
        +addDependency(Action*)
        +prepare()
        +calculate()
        +apply()
        +update()
    }
    class "ActionAtomistic (src/core/ActionAtomistic.h)" {
        +requestAtoms(vector<AtomNumber>)
        +getPosition(int): Vector
        +setForces(vector<Vector>)
    }
    class "ActionWithValue (src/core/ActionWithValue.h)" {
        +getValue(string): Value*
        +addValue(string)
        +setDerivatives()
    }
    class "ActionWithArguments (src/core/ActionWithArguments.h)" {
        +parseArgumentList()
        +getArgument(int): Value*
    }
    class "ActionPilot (src/core/ActionPilot.h)" {
        +getStride(): int
        +onStep(): bool
    }

    "Action" <|-- "ActionAtomistic"
    "Action" <|-- "ActionWithValue"
    "Action" <|-- "ActionWithArguments"
    "Action" <|-- "ActionPilot"
```
Sources: [src/core/Action.h](), [src/core/ActionAtomistic.h](), [src/core/ActionWithArguments.cpp]()

This diagram maps the main Action-related classes to their code locations and highlights their main methods.

## Action Registration

Actions are registered with the framework using the `ActionRegister` singleton. Registration is typically performed at static initialization time using the `PLUMED_REGISTER_ACTION` macro, which associates an action name (as used in input files) with a C++ class.

**Diagram: Action Registration and Lookup**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "PluginCode" as "Plugin Code"
    participant "ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)" as "ActionRegister"
    participant "PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)" as "PlumedMain"

    "PluginCode"->>"ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)": "PLUMED_REGISTER_ACTION(ActionClass, \"ActionName\")"
    Note over "PluginCode","ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)": "Static registration at startup"
    "PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)"}->>"ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)": "create(actionName, options)"
    "ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)"->>"ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)": "Find creator function"
    "ActionRegister (src/core/ActionRegister.h)"->>"PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)": "Return ActionClass instance"
```
Sources: [src/core/ActionRegister.cpp:39-66](), [src/core/ActionRegister.h]()

This mechanism allows PLUMED to instantiate the correct C++ class for each action specified in the input file.

## Action Creation Process

When PLUMED parses the input file, it creates Actions using the following steps:

1. Read a line from the input file.
2. Extract the action name (first word).
3. Look up the action creator in `ActionRegister`.
4. Prepare an `ActionOptions` object with the parsed line.
5. Call the creator function to instantiate the Action.
6. Add the Action to the `ActionSet`.

**Diagram: Action Instantiation from Input**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Parse input line [e.g. 'DISTANCE ATOMS=1,2 LABEL=d12']"] --> B["Extract action name ['DISTANCE']"]
    B --> C["Look up creator in ActionRegister"]
    C --> D["Create ActionOptions"]
    D --> E["Call creator function"]
    E --> F["Constructor registers keywords"]
    F --> G["Constructor parses input"]
    G --> H["Constructor initializes action"]
    H --> I["Add to ActionSet"]
```
Sources: [src/core/ActionRegister.cpp:39-66](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:285-604]()

This process is managed by `PlumedMain` and ensures that each input line results in a properly constructed Action object.

## Action Lifecycle

Each Action instance follows a well-defined lifecycle, coordinated by `PlumedMain`:

1. **Registration**: The Action class is registered with `ActionRegister`.
2. **Creation**: An instance is created during input parsing.
3. **Initialization**: The Action sets up internal data structures.
4. **Preparation**: The Action prepares for calculation (e.g., checks dependencies, sets up atom lists).
5. **Calculation**: The Action performs its computation.
6. **Application**: Results (such as forces) are applied to the system.
7. **Update**: The Action updates its internal state.

`PlumedMain` orchestrates these phases by calling the appropriate methods on each Action.

Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:347-435](), [src/core/PlumedMain.h:346-361]()

## Action Dependencies

Actions can depend on the results of other Actions, forming a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of dependencies. This ensures that calculations are performed in the correct order.

**Diagram: Example of Action Dependency Graph**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["DISTANCE ATOMS=1,2 LABEL=d12"] --> C["METAD ARG=d12,t1234"]
    B["TORSION ATOMS=1,2,3,4 LABEL=t1234"] --> C
```

Dependencies are established using the `addDependency` method in the `Action` class:

```cpp
void Action::addDependency(Action* a) {
  after.push_back(a);
}
```
Sources: [src/core/Action.cpp:140-145](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:347-435]()

`PlumedMain` uses these dependencies to determine the correct execution order for all Actions.

## Execution Phases

During each simulation step, Actions are executed in a series of phases, coordinated by `PlumedMain`:

1. **prepareDependencies**: Determine which Actions are active and their dependencies.
2. **prepareCalc**: Prepare Actions for calculation.
3. **performCalc**: Execute the calculation for all active Actions.
4. **apply**: Apply results (e.g., forces) to the system.
5. **update**: Update the internal state of Actions.

**Diagram: Action Execution Sequence**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "MD Engine"
    participant "PlumedMain"
    participant "Action1"
    participant "Action2"

    "MD Engine"->>"PlumedMain": cmd("calc", NULL)
    "PlumedMain"->>"PlumedMain": prepareDependencies()
    "PlumedMain"->>"Action1": prepare()
    "Action1"->>"PlumedMain": done
    "PlumedMain"->>"Action2": prepare()
    "Action2"->>"PlumedMain": done

    "PlumedMain"->>"Action1": calculate()
    "Action1"->>"PlumedMain": done
    "PlumedMain"->>"Action2": calculate()
    "Action2"->>"PlumedMain": done

    "PlumedMain"->>"Action2": apply()
    "Action2"->>"PlumedMain": done
    "PlumedMain"->>"Action1": apply()
    "Action1"->>"PlumedMain": done

    "PlumedMain"->>"Action1": update()
    "Action1"->>"PlumedMain": done
    "PlumedMain"->>"Action2": update()
    "Action2"->>"PlumedMain": done
    "PlumedMain"->>"MD Engine": return
```
Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:347-435](), [src/core/PlumedMain.h:346-361]()

## Keywords System

Actions define their input parameters using the `Keywords` system, which provides a structured way to declare, document, and validate input options.

**Diagram: Keywords System Entities**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "Keywords (src/tools/Keywords.h)" {
        +add(type, key, docstring)
        +addFlag(key, defaultValue, docstring)
        +reserve(type, key, docstring)
        +getStyle(key): string
        +getDefaultValue(key, value): bool
    }
    class "KeyType"
    class "keyInfo" {
        +type: KeyType
        +docstring: string
        +defaultValue: variant
        +allowmultiple: bool
    }

    "Keywords (src/tools/Keywords.h)" o-- "KeyType"
    "Keywords (src/tools/Keywords.h)" o-- "keyInfo"
```
Sources: [src/tools/Keywords.h](), [src/tools/Keywords.cpp:55-108]()

When registering keywords, Actions specify:
- Required parameters (compulsory)
- Optional parameters
- Flags (boolean switches)
- Default values
- Documentation strings

This system is used both for input validation and for generating user documentation.

## Implementation Pattern for Actions

To implement a new Action in PLUMED, developers follow a standard pattern:

1. Define a class inheriting from the appropriate Action base classes.
2. Register keywords using the `registerKeywords` static method.
3. Implement the constructor to parse input options.
4. Implement the `calculate` method for the computation.
5. Register the Action using `PLUMED_REGISTER_ACTION`.

**Diagram: Action Implementation Workflow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Define Action class (inherits from Action or subclasses)"] --> B["Implement registerKeywords()"]
    B --> C["Implement constructor"]
    C --> D["Implement calculate()"]
    D --> E["Register with PLUMED_REGISTER_ACTION"]
```
Sources: [src/colvar/Distance.cpp](), [src/core/ActionRegister.cpp]()

This pattern ensures consistency and integration with the Action Framework.

## Integration with PlumedMain

The Action Framework is orchestrated by the `PlumedMain` class, which acts as the central coordinator for input parsing, action management, and simulation control.

**Diagram: Integration of PlumedMain, ActionSet, and Action**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)" {
        +actionSet: ActionSet
        +cmd(key: string, val: TypesafePtr)
        +readInputFile(file: string)
        +init()
        +prepareCalc()
        +performCalc()
        +update()
    }
    class "ActionSet (src/core/ActionSet.h)" {
        +emplace_back(Action*)
        +select<T>(): vector<T*>
        +pushBack(Action*)
        +selectWithLabel<T>(label): T*
    }
    class "Action (src/core/Action.h)" {
        +plumed: PlumedMain&
        +calculate()
        +apply()
        +update()
    }

    "PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)" o-- "ActionSet (src/core/ActionSet.h)"
    "ActionSet (src/core/ActionSet.h)" o-- "Action (src/core/Action.h)"
    "Action (src/core/Action.h)" -- "PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)"
```
Sources: [src/core/PlumedMain.h:74-430](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-885]()

`PlumedMain` provides the interface between the MD engine and the Action Framework, handling:
- Input file parsing and Action creation
- The MD-PLUMED communication protocol
- Coordinating the execution of Actions
- Managing the simulation lifecycle

## TypesafePtr System

The Action Framework uses the `TypesafePtr` system to safely pass data between components, especially at the interface between PLUMED and the MD engine. This system provides runtime type checking and ensures memory safety.

**Diagram: TypesafePtr Usage in PlumedMain**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "TypesafePtr (src/tools/TypesafePtr.h)" {
        +get<T>(): T
        +set<T>(value: T)
        +getCString(): const char*
        +copy(): TypesafePtr
    }
    class "PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)" {
        +cmd(key: string, val: TypesafePtr)
    }

    "PlumedMain (src/core/PlumedMain.h)" -- "TypesafePtr (src/tools/TypesafePtr.h)"
```
Sources: [src/tools/TypesafePtr.h](), [src/core/PlumedMain.cpp:313-377]()

This system ensures that data passed to and from Actions is properly typed and sized, preventing memory corruption and type errors.

## Conclusion

The Action Framework is the backbone of PLUMED, providing a flexible, extensible system for implementing a wide range of molecular simulation analyses and enhanced sampling methods. By following a standard pattern and utilizing the framework's capabilities, developers can add new functionality to PLUMED in a structured, maintainable way.

Understanding the Action Framework is essential for both using PLUMED effectively and extending it with new capabilities. The modular design allows for complex calculations to be broken down into simple, composable Actions that can be combined in various ways to implement sophisticated analysis and simulation techniques.

---

# Exception Handling

This page documents the error and exception handling mechanisms within the PLUMED codebase. Exception handling in PLUMED is designed to provide robust, context-rich error reporting for both developers and users, with detailed messages, file/line/function information, and optional stack traces. The system is tightly integrated with the build and quality system, and is enforced by code quality tools.

---

## Exception Class Hierarchy and Code Entities

PLUMED implements a custom exception system based on C++ exceptions. The main class is `PLMD::Exception`, which derives from `std::exception`. Several specialized exception types are provided for different error categories.

**Exception Class Hierarchy Diagram**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    "std::exception" <|-- "PLMD::Exception"
    "PLMD::Exception" <|-- "PLMD::ExceptionError"
    "PLMD::Exception" <|-- "PLMD::ExceptionDebug"
    "PLMD::Exception" <|-- "PLMD::ExceptionTypeError"

    class "PLMD::Exception" {
      - "std::string msg"
      - "std::stringstream stream"
      - "std::array<void*,128> callstack"
      - "int callstack_n"
      - "std::string stackTrace"
      + "what() const"
      + "stack() const"
      + "operator<<(const std::string&)"
      + "operator<<(const Location&)"
      + "operator<<(const Assertion&)"
    }
    class "PLMD::ExceptionError" {
      + "operator<<(const T&)"
    }
    class "PLMD::ExceptionDebug" {
      + "operator<<(const T&)"
    }
    class "PLMD::ExceptionTypeError" {
      + "operator<<(const T&)"
    }
```

**Key code entities:**
- `PLMD::Exception`
- `PLMD::ExceptionError`
- `PLMD::ExceptionDebug`
- `PLMD::ExceptionTypeError`

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:155-332]()

## Exception Flow and Propagation

When an error condition is detected, a `PLMD::Exception` (or derived type) is created and thrown. Contextual information (file, line, function) is attached automatically via macros. Exceptions propagate up the call stack and can be caught at any level.

**Exception Propagation Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "DetectError"["Code detects error condition"] --> "CreateException"["PLMD::Exception or derived type is created"]
    "CreateException" --> "AddContext"["File, line, function info added (via macros)"]
    "AddContext" --> "ThrowException"["Exception is thrown"]
    "ThrowException" --> "Propagate"["Exception propagates up call stack"]
    "Propagate" --> "Catch?"{"Is exception caught?"}
    "Catch?" -- "Yes" --> "Handle"["Exception is handled (e.g., error message displayed)"]
    "Catch?" -- "No" --> "Terminate"["Program terminates with error message"]
```

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:135-146](), [src/cltools/Driver.cpp:640-643]()

## Exception Macros and Context Injection

PLUMED provides macros to simplify exception throwing and ensure that context (file, line, function) is always included. These macros are the standard way to report errors and assertions in the codebase.

| Macro | Description | Typical Usage |
|-------|-------------|--------------|
| `plumed_error()` | Throws a `PLMD::ExceptionError` with file/line/function info | `plumed_error() << "Failed to read file";` |
| `plumed_merror(msg)` | Same as above, but takes a message as argument | `plumed_merror("Failed to read file");` |
| `plumed_assert(test)` | Throws if `test` is false, with context | `plumed_assert(a > 0) << "a must be positive";` |
| `plumed_massert(test, msg)` | Throws if `test` is false, with message | `plumed_massert(a > 0, "a must be positive");` |
| `plumed_dbg_assert(test)` | Like `plumed_assert`, but only in debug builds | `plumed_dbg_assert(expensive_check());` |
| `plumed_dbg_massert(test, msg)` | Like `plumed_massert`, but only in debug builds | `plumed_dbg_massert(expensive_check(), "check failed");` |

All macros automatically inject file, line, and function information using the `plumed_here` macro, which creates a `PLMD::Exception::Location` object.

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:350-402]()

## Error Message Construction and Insertion Operator

The `PLMD::Exception` class supports the insertion operator (`<<`) for building detailed error messages. This allows developers to append arbitrary information, including variable values, to the exception message in a type-safe way.

**Error Message Construction Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "ErrorDetected"["Error detected"] --> "CreateException"["Create PLMD::Exception"]
    "CreateException" --> "AddContext"["Add file/line/function info (via macro)"]
    "AddContext" --> "AddMessage"["Add custom message via <<"]
    "AddMessage" --> "AddValues"["Add variable values via <<"]
    "AddValues" --> "Throw"["Throw the exception"]
```

**Example Usage:**
- `plumed_error() << "Failed to read file";`
- `plumed_error() << "Invalid value: " << value;`
- `plumed_assert(a > 0) << "a must be positive, got a=" << a;`

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:86-111]()

## Stack Traces

PLUMED exceptions can include a stack trace, which is useful for debugging. Stack traces are captured using `backtrace` and `backtrace_symbols` (when available) and are included in the error message if the environment variable `PLUMED_STACK_TRACE` is set to `yes` at runtime.

**How to Enable Stack Traces:**
```sh
export PLUMED_STACK_TRACE=yes
```

When enabled, the stack trace is appended to the exception message.

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.cpp:86-96]()

## Exception Handling in Application and Library Code

Exceptions can be caught and handled at various levels. In command-line tools (e.g., `Driver`), exceptions are caught and error messages are printed to the user. In library usage, external codes can catch PLUMED exceptions as `std::exception`.

**Example:**
```cpp
try {
    plumed.cmd("calc");
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "Error: %s\n", e.what());
    return 1;
}
```

In some cases (e.g., MPI environments), exceptions may trigger program termination.

Sources: [src/tools/Communicator.cpp:127-135](), [src/cltools/Driver.cpp:640-643]()

## Exception Safety and Resource Management

PLUMED code is written to provide basic exception safety. Resource management is typically handled using RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) patterns, such as `std::unique_ptr` with custom deleters for file handles and other resources. This ensures that resources are released even if an exception is thrown.

**Example:**
```cpp
std::unique_ptr<FILE, decltype(deleter)> fp_deleter(fp, deleter);
```

Sources: [src/cltools/Driver.cpp:349-356](), [src/cltools/SimpleMD.cpp:78-82]()

## Location and Assertion Information in Exceptions

The `PLMD::Exception` class contains nested classes for storing context:

- `PLMD::Exception::Location`: Stores file, line, and function name.
- `PLMD::Exception::Assertion`: Stores the failed assertion expression.
- `PLMD::Exception::Throw`: Used for nested exception support.

**Location and Assertion Class Diagram**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    "PLMD::Exception" o-- "PLMD::Exception::Location"
    "PLMD::Exception" o-- "PLMD::Exception::Assertion"
    "PLMD::Exception" o-- "PLMD::Exception::Throw"

    class "PLMD::Exception::Location" {
      + "const char* file"
      + "const unsigned line"
      + "const char* pretty"
      + "Location(file, line, pretty)"
    }
    class "PLMD::Exception::Assertion" {
      + "const char* assertion"
      + "Assertion(assertion)"
    }
    class "PLMD::Exception::Throw" {
      + "operator<<=()"
    }
```

The `plumed_here` macro creates a `Location` object with the current file, line, and function name.

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:173-195](), [src/tools/Exception.h:350-351]()

## Nested Exceptions

PLUMED supports nested exceptions using the C++11 `std::throw_with_nested` mechanism. This allows error context to be preserved across multiple layers of function calls.

**Nested Exception Propagation**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "LowLevelThrow"["Low-level function throws exception"] --> "MidLevelCatch"["Mid-level function catches exception"]
    "MidLevelCatch" --> "MidLevelThrowNested"["Mid-level function throws nested exception"]
    "MidLevelThrowNested" --> "HighLevelCatch"["High-level function catches nested exception"]
    "HighLevelCatch" --> "Report"["Error is reported with full context chain"]
```

The `plumed_error_nested()` macro is used to throw nested exceptions.

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:202-214](), [src/tools/Exception.h:364-365]()

## Error vs. Assertion Macros

PLUMED distinguishes between errors and assertions:

- **Errors** (`plumed_error`, `plumed_merror`): Used for conditions that should not occur in correct code, but may happen due to external factors (e.g., invalid input).
- **Assertions** (`plumed_assert`, `plumed_massert`): Used to check programming invariants that should never be violated.

**Decision Flow: Error or Assertion**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "IsInvariant"["Is the condition an invariant that should always be true?"] -- "Yes" --> "UseAssert"["Use assertion (plumed_assert)"]
    "IsInvariant" -- "No" --> "IsExpectedError"["Is it an expected error condition?"]
    "IsExpectedError" -- "Yes" --> "HandleNormally"["Handle normally (if/else)"]
    "IsExpectedError" -- "No" --> "UseError"["Use error (plumed_error)"]
```

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:95-104]()

## Debug Assertions

Debug assertions (`plumed_dbg_assert`, `plumed_dbg_massert`) are only active in debug builds (when `NDEBUG` is not defined). These are intended for expensive or development-only checks.

**Example:**
```cpp
plumed_dbg_assert(expensive_function(i) > 0) << "Value must be positive";
```

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:384-402]()

## Exception Handling in External Code

When PLUMED is used as a library in external code, exceptions can be caught and handled by the external code. This allows for graceful error handling and recovery.

```cpp
try {
    plumed.cmd("setPrecision", n);
} catch (const std::exception & e) {
    std::printf("PLUMED error: %s", e.what());
    exit(1);
}
```

Sources: [src/tools/Exception.h:132-140](src/tools/Exception.h:132-140)

# Page: Enhanced Sampling Methods

# Enhanced Sampling Methods

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This document provides a comprehensive overview of the enhanced sampling methods implemented in PLUMED. Enhanced sampling methods help overcome energy barriers in molecular dynamics simulations, allowing for more efficient exploration of the conformational space and calculation of free energies. PLUMED offers a variety of these methods with different strengths and applications.

For implementation details on specific enhanced sampling methods, see their dedicated pages:
- [Metadynamics (3.1)](#3.1)
- [OPES (3.2)](#3.2)
- [DRR and eABF (3.3)](#3.3)
- [VES (3.4)](#3.4)

## Enhanced Sampling Methods Overview

Enhanced sampling methods in PLUMED are designed to accelerate the exploration of free energy landscapes by applying bias forces to selected collective variables. These methods overcome the limitations of standard molecular dynamics simulations, which can get trapped in local energy minima for extended periods.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Enhanced Sampling Methods"
        MetaD["Metadynamics\n(MetaD, PBMetaD)"]
        OPES["On-the-fly Probability\nEnhanced Sampling\n(OPES)"]
        DRR["Dynamic Reference\nRestraining\n(DRR/eABF)"]
        VES["Variational Enhanced\nSampling\n(VES)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Common Mechanisms"
        CV["Collective Variables"]
        Bias["Bias Potential"]
        FES["Free Energy Surface"]
    end
    
    CV --> Bias
    Bias --> FES
    
    MetaD --> Bias
    OPES --> Bias
    DRR --> Bias
    VES --> Bias
    
    style MetaD fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style OPES fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style DRR fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style VES fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style CV fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style Bias fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style FES fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
```

Sources: [src/bias/MetaD.cpp](). [src/bias/PBMetaD.cpp](). [src/opes/OPESmetad.cpp](). [src/opes/OPESexpanded.cpp](). [src/drr/DynamicReferenceRestraining.cpp]().

## Metadynamics

Metadynamics enhances sampling by adding a history-dependent bias potential composed of Gaussian functions to discourage the system from revisiting already sampled configurations. 

In standard metadynamics, the bias potential is given by:

$$V(\vec{s},t) = \sum_{ k \tau < t} W(k \tau) \exp\left(-\sum_{i=1}^{d} \frac{(s_i-s_i^{(0)}(k \tau))^2}{2\sigma_i^2}\right)$$

This bias gradually fills energy minima, pushing the system to explore new regions of the configurational space.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    Bias <|-- MetaD
    Bias <|-- PBMetaD
    Bias <|-- OPES_METAD
    Bias <|-- DRR
    
    class Bias {
        <<Abstract>>
        +calculate()
        +update()
    }
    
    class MetaD {
        -hills_
        -grid_
        +addGaussian()
        +calculate()
        +update()
    }
    
    class PBMetaD {
        -hills_[]
        -grids_[]
        +calculate()
        +update()
    }
    
    class OPES_METAD {
        -kernels_
        -compress()
        +calculate()
        +update()
    }
    
    class DRR {
        -fictNoPBC_
        -real_
        -fbias_
        +calculate()
        +update()
    }
```

Sources: [src/bias/MetaD.cpp:482-633](). [src/bias/PBMetaD.cpp:238-337](). [src/opes/OPESmetad.cpp:166-250](). [src/drr/DynamicReferenceRestraining.cpp:180-243]().

### Well-Tempered Metadynamics

A popular variant of metadynamics is well-tempered metadynamics, where the height of Gaussian hills decreases with time according to:

$$W(k\tau) = W_0 e^{-V(s,k\tau)/\Delta T}$$

This ensures that the bias potential converges more smoothly to the negative of the free energy.

### Multiple Walker Metadynamics

PLUMED also supports multiple walker approaches where several simulations (walkers) contribute to the same bias potential, enhancing convergence through collaborative sampling.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Metadynamics Variants"
        Standard["Standard Metadynamics"]
        WellTemp["Well-Tempered\nMetadynamics"]
        PBM["Parallel Bias\nMetadynamics"]
        Multi["Multiple Walkers\nMetadynamics"]
        Transition["Transition-Tempered\nMetadynamics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Implementation Components"
        Hills["Gaussian Hills\nRepresentation"]
        Grids["Grid Storage"]
        NList["Neighbor Lists"]
        Reweighting["Reweighting Tools"]
    end
    
    Standard --> Hills
    WellTemp --> Hills
    PBM --> Hills
    Multi --> Hills
    Transition --> Hills
    
    Hills --> Grids
    Grids --> NList
    Hills --> Reweighting
    
    style Standard fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style WellTemp fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style PBM fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style Multi fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style Transition fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style Hills fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style Grids fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style NList fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style Reweighting fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
```

Sources: [src/bias/MetaD.cpp:187-207](). [src/bias/MetaD.cpp:291-317](). [src/bias/PBMetaD.cpp:40-95](). [src/bias/PBMetaD.cpp:195-234]().

## On-the-fly Probability Enhanced Sampling (OPES)

OPES is a more recent enhanced sampling method that optimizes the bias on-the-fly through probability density estimation. Two main variants are implemented:

### OPES_METAD

This variant uses a metadynamics-like target distribution with the bias at step n given by:

$$V_n(\mathbf{s}) = (1-1/\gamma)\frac{1}{\beta}\log\left(\frac{P_n(\mathbf{s})}{Z_n}+\epsilon\right)$$

OPES_METAD aims to quickly get a coarse estimate of the full free energy surface and then refine its details. It uses a compression algorithm to limit the number of kernels.

### OPES_EXPANDED

This variant works with expanded ensembles, allowing simulation of multiple thermodynamic conditions. The bias is:

$$V_n(\mathbf{x})=-\frac{1}{\beta}\log \left(\frac{1}{N_{\{\lambda\}}}\sum_\lambda e^{-\Delta u_\lambda(\mathbf{x})+\beta\Delta F_n(\lambda)}\right)$$

This allows for sampling a range of temperatures, pressures, or other conditions within a single simulation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "OPES Variants"
        OPES_M["OPES_METAD\n(Metadynamics-like target)"]
        OPES_E["OPES_EXPANDED\n(Expanded ensemble target)"]
        OPES_ME["OPES_METAD_EXPLORE\n(Exploration mode)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Expansion Collective Variables"
        ECV_MT["ECV_MULTITHERMAL\n(Multiple temperatures)"]
        ECV_MTB["ECV_MULTITHERMAL_MULTIBARIC\n(Multiple temperatures & pressures)"]
        ECV_UL["ECV_UMBRELLAS_LINE\n(Umbrella sampling along line)"]
        ECV_UF["ECV_UMBRELLAS_FILE\n(Umbrella sampling from file)"]
    end
    
    OPES_E --> ECV_MT
    OPES_E --> ECV_MTB
    OPES_E --> ECV_UL
    OPES_E --> ECV_UF
    
    style OPES_M fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style OPES_E fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style OPES_ME fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style ECV_MT fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style ECV_MTB fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style ECV_UL fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style ECV_UF fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
```

Sources: [src/opes/OPESmetad.cpp:29-164](). [src/opes/OPESmetad.cpp:261-297](). [src/opes/OPESexpanded.cpp:32-113](). [src/opes/ECVmultiThermal.cpp](). [src/opes/ECVmultiThermalBaric.cpp:25-72](). [src/opes/ECVumbrellasLine.cpp](). [src/opes/ECVumbrellasFile.cpp]().

## Dynamic Reference Restraining (DRR)

DRR, also known as extended-system Adaptive Biasing Force (eABF), attaches fictitious variables to collective variables through springs. The bias force acts on the fictitious variables rather than directly on the collective variables.

For each collective variable \(ξ_i\), a fictitious variable \(λ_i\) is attached through a spring. The bias force on \(λ_i\) is the negative average spring force, enhancing the sampling of \(λ_i\):

$$F_{bias}(λ_i) = k(λ_i - \langle ξ_i \rangle_{λ_i})$$

DRR supports multiple estimators:
- Naïve (ABF) estimator: negative average spring force
- CZAR (Corrected z-averaged restraint) estimator
- UI (Umbrella Integration) estimator

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "DRR/eABF Components"
        ABFGrid["ABFGrid"]
        CZAR["CZAR Estimator"]
        UI["UI Estimator"]
        Langevin["Extended Langevin\nDynamics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "DRR Implementation"
        drrMain["DynamicReferenceRestraining\nClass"]
        ABF["ABF on Fictitious\nVariables"]
        Biasforces["Bias Forces"]
        OutputFiles["Output Files\n(.drrstate, .grad, .count)"]
    end
    
    drrMain --> ABFGrid
    drrMain --> CZAR
    drrMain --> UI
    drrMain --> Langevin
    
    ABFGrid --> ABF
    CZAR --> Biasforces
    UI --> Biasforces
    Langevin --> Biasforces
    Biasforces --> OutputFiles
    
    style drrMain fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style ABFGrid fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    style CZAR fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
```
